We have been given the following diagonalization of $A.$

$$
A={{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{P}{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{D}{{{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}}_{⏟}}_{{P}^{-1}}
$$

So, since $A=PD{P}^{-1}$, we can compute ${A}^{k}$ by using the formula 

$$
{A}^{k}=P{D}^{k}{P}^{-1}.
$$

First, we find the inverse of the matrix $P.$ We get

$$
{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}=\frac{1}{-2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]=-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$

Carrying out the necessary multiplication, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{85} & =P{D}^{85}{P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}^{85}{[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{1}^{85} & 0 \\ 0 & (-1)^{85}\end{aligned}](-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
